title: POC Weekly Sync: Throughput/Latency Results + Routing Playbook Handoff
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review sprint results (latency and throughput) versus the incumbent baseline, decide routing/fallback playbook, and hand off next steps for Dedicated slot request and security docs. SE presented bench numbers and proposed routing thresholds; customer asked for unit-cost comparison and an on-prem quantization run. Action items assigned and plan to run a head-to-head 1-hour load test next Tuesday.
action_items: Devon Patel: Share the per-token unit cost spreadsheet + baseline calc (due 2026-07-16)
Maya Chen: Put together Dedicated slot proposal and pricing tiers (due 2026-07-20)
Hannah Lee: Provide sample traffic shape (p95/p99 payloads) and expected QPS for head-to-head (due 2026-07-15)
Rajiv Kapoor: Approve test window for 1-hour load run next Tue 07/20 (due 2026-07-17)
Eloise Park: Send SOC2 + data residency notes and link to security pack (due 2026-07-14)
next_steps: Run 1-hour head-to-head load test (Redwood vs Incumbent) during agreed window
Redwood to provide Dedicated slot pricing and options
Customer to try on-prem quantize job on sample model and share logs
Schedule technical deep-dive on routing rules if head-to-head delta > 10ms p50
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-07-13 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 min | Recording by Fireflies
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Eloise Park (Redwood CSM), Rajiv Kapoor (Sundial Head of ML), Hannah Lee (Sundial Platform), Tom Alvarez (Sundial CTO), Marta Ruiz (Sundial SRE)

Summary: Quick recap of week 3 bench results, routing playbook draft, and next steps for Dedicated slot and compliance packet handoff.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we were hoping to keep this tight 45-ish minutes, we have Devon to run through the numbers then we can triage routing playbook and next steps.
[00:12] Rajiv Kapoor: yeah sounds good, thanks Maya. morning from our side.
[00:15] Devon Patel: okay, i'll share my screen in a sec, i'll just jump into the bench results. quick note some of the numbers are noisy, we had a couple of cold starts in the first run, we dropped those out.
[00:28] Devon Patel: slide 1: p50/p95 latency across 512-token avg prompts, Redwood configured with batching=32, prefix cache enabled, quantized to int8 on the candidate model. p50 is 42ms vs incumbent 68ms; p95 is 210ms vs incumbent 280ms. throughput steady at 850 r/s sustained vs incumbent 540 r/s on the same hardware footprint.
[01:02] Hannah Lee: can i clarify the hardware — that was the g4x-1 equivalent? we run our own benches on g4x-like instances.
[01:08] Devon Patel: good callout. this was run on a 4x A100 equivalent cluster for Redwood's Dedicated slot emulation; incumbent runs were provided by Sundial and normalized to the same vram/cores per node. there is a normalization factor included in the sheet.
[01:26] Tom Alvarez: normalization — is that per-token or per-second? i want to make sure apples-to-apples.
[01:31] Devon Patel: per-second; we normalized QPS by raw FLOP equivalence and verified with a small head-to-head microbench. there may be +/- 5% error, but directionally the delta is consistent.
[01:46] Rajiv Kapoor: the p95 gap matters for us — our SLA is 300ms for inference 99th for user-facing flows; curious how much of that p95 is queuing vs model compute.
[01:57] Devon Patel: right — our traces show about 60% of p95 delta is model compute long tail, 30% is batching queuing, and 10% is network/jitter. with continuous batching set to aggressive we see better throughput but p95 creeps up for bursty patterns.
[02:18] Marta Ruiz: how is KV cache performing? i saw in the notes you mentioned kv-cash, sorry kv cache.
[02:24] Devon Patel: ha, yes, kv cache — we saw a 12-18% effective token saving for repeated session prefixes due to prefix caching; when the workload is highly sessionized we get huge wins. if you're mostly stateless micro-prompts the cache benefit is smaller.
[02:42] Hannah Lee: our work is mixed — about 40% sessionized, 60% stateless short prompts. so what would real-world be?
[02:50] Devon Patel: you should expect somewhere between 5-10% token savings on average given your mix. we'll send the simulated traffic run with your p95/p99 shapes; that will show effective savings.
[03:05] Maya Chen: quick commercial / unit-cost note — Devon shared a unit-cost calc sheet that shows Redwood's per-token cost at current config is ~0.0009 USD/token compared to incumbent at ~0.0016 after their bulk discounts. i'll let devon expand.
[03:20] Devon Patel: yes that's the ballpark. the big drivers are batching and idle packing. incumbent is conservative on batching so their cost per token is higher at same latency SLO.
[03:33] Tom Alvarez: those numbers look promising but we need the spreadsheet with the assumptions, like duty cycle, average seq length, etc.
[03:40] Devon Patel: absolutely, i'll drop that as a follow-up (Devon: points to shared drive).
[03:46] Rajiv Kapoor: can you also show head-to-head traces — like a small 15-minute run?
[03:50] Devon Patel: yes we proposed a 1-hour head-to-head next week to get stable numbers.
[03:55] Eloise Park: from an ops hand-off perspective, after the head-to-head we'll recommend a routing plan and a canary window. that's part of the playbook.
[04:05] Maya Chen: ok let's walk routing playbook draft. Devon?
[04:08] Devon Patel: slide: routing playbook v0. key idea — route by latency sensitivity: tier A (user-facing chat) -> low-latency nodes/dedicated slots; tier B (async batch or embeddings) -> cost-optimized pool; tier C fallback -> smaller quantized model for extreme surge. set thresholds: if p50 exceeds 60ms or p95 exceeds 250ms for 2 consecutive minutes, switch 15% of traffic back to incumbent or to fallback model depending on cost/latency profile.
[04:44] Hannah Lee: switching to incumbent is tricky for us due to data residency and SSO, we prefer fallback to smaller quantized model within our VPC.
[04:51] Maya Chen: that's totally fine, routing can be configured to prefer in-region fallback variants. the canary and gradual rollouts are configurable in Console.
[04:59] Tom Alvarez: about the fallback model — how different is quality after int8 quant? our NLU accuracy is sensitive.
[05:07] Devon Patel: good question, we ran evals on your standard prompt set — BLEU-ish metric/label accuracy dips 1.8% on average for int8 4-bit hybrid, and for aggressive quant it can be 3-5%. granular evals are in the eval folder.
[05:25] Rajiv Kapoor: 1.8% might be acceptable if latency wins are big. need to see case-by-case.
[05:29] Marta Ruiz: can we throttle what parts of traffic go to fallback? like only non-critical intents?
[05:34] Devon Patel: yes, routing rules can include classifiers or header tags to route by intent. we can ship a rule prototype that uses header flagging — very common pattern.
[05:43] Hannah Lee: on the topic of security — we need SAML SSO + audit logs + KMS integration for keys. you mentioned a private deployment option, what is timeline for that?
[05:54] Maya Chen: Private (VPC) path is an option; typical timeline is 6-8 weeks for onboarding with SOC2 + KMS integration if everything's green. Eloise will send the security pack and a checklist.
[06:06] Eloise Park: i'll share SOC2, ISO summary, and our standard KMS integration doc after the call. there are small items for the network team but we can work with your SRE.
[06:15] Tom Alvarez: great.
[06:18] Devon Patel: back to the bench: number caveats — we saw tail variance when we increased batching aggressiveness from 32 to 64; throughput improved 20% but p95 increased 40-60ms in bursty patterns. so recommended default: batching=32 and adaptive batching thresholds for burst detection.
[06:37] Rajiv Kapoor: are those adaptive thresholds controlled in Console or config API?
[06:41] Devon Patel: both. Console has sliders for latency vs cost, API allows exact thresholds and can be tied to tracing.
[06:47] Hannah Lee: can we get the trace logs around the cold start event you mentioned?
[06:51] Devon Patel: yes, i'll annotate the run and share.
[06:54] Maya Chen: can we discuss Dedicated slot ask? Rajiv said earlier you might want reserved capacity. Rajiv?
[06:59] Rajiv Kapoor: yes, if Redwood keeps these deltas we want dedicated nodes to guarantee throughput. need pricing and SLA.
[07:06] Maya Chen: Devon and I will propose a Dedicated slot tiered pricing. we have reserved capacity monthly/quarterly options, with an SLA for p50/p95. i'll price two options: minimal reserved to cover peak 90th and full reserved.
[07:18] Tom Alvarez: about burst protection — can you offer burst capacity?
[07:21] Maya Chen: yes we have burst pools; can be attached to Dedicated with defined burst throttle limits.
[07:26] Marta Ruiz: are the audit logs PII-filtered by default? we need to not send raw user data externally.
[07:31] Eloise Park: logs can be redacted; we also support streaming audit logs to your SIEM. we'll include those options in the security packet.
[07:41] Rajiv Kapoor: let's talk about the head-to-head — we want to run at our ingress with real traffic replay for 1 hour, can Redwood provide a drop-in routing to route 20% traffic to Redwood during test?
[07:52] Devon Patel: yes we can provide a canary config and a small client agent to hit Redwood endpoints under your VPC or ours. we'll need the traffic shape and the window.
[07:59] Hannah Lee: we'll share traffic replay and a 1-hour window Tues 07/20 02:00-03:00 UTC, pending internal approvals.
[08:07] Maya Chen: great, we've tentatively scheduled that.
[08:12] Tom Alvarez: one last technical — we saw an incumbent claim about faster KV cache warmup; any strategy to improve warmup for session-ized traffic?
[08:21] Devon Patel: warmup can be improved with prefetching and priming — Redwood supports a prewarm API that lets you load prefix KV state ahead of route cutover. we can coordinate with your session orchestrator to prime likely prefixes. that reduced p95 by ~30ms in our tests.
[08:37] Rajiv Kapoor: nice.
[08:39] Devon Patel: small note on telemetry — if you're instrumenting traces, please pass the request-id header we can mirror and we can supply trace correlation. that helps with root cause.
[08:49] Maya Chen: ok moving to open Q's — Hannah?
[08:53] Hannah Lee: can you confirm encryption at rest key management — do you support customer-managed keys in the private path?
[08:59] Eloise Park: yes, on Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; Hosted also supports BYOK for enterprise with contract. we'll detail in packet.
[09:09] Hannah Lee: good.
[09:11] Rajiv Kapoor: another commercial point — if we commit to 6 months reserved, what discount band would we expect?
[09:18] Maya Chen: we'll include tiered discounts at 3/6/12 month commitments in the Dedicated proposal.
[09:25] Tom Alvarez: back to routing: is manual override possible for live incidents to route everything to fallback?
[09:31] Devon Patel: yes, manual overrides via Console and API; also we support automated fallback based on anomaly detection.
[09:38] Marta Ruiz: do you support audit trails for overrides?
[09:41] Eloise Park: yes every override is an auditable event with user and timestamp.
[09:46] Maya Chen: we're at about the 30-minute mark, should we quick recap and then wrap?
[09:51] Rajiv Kapoor: quick recap please.
[09:53] Maya Chen: recap: 1) Redwood p50/p95 and throughput look favorable vs incumbent for our test cases; 2) routing playbook v0 proposed with fallback to quantized models in-region preferred by Sundial; 3) Dedicated slot pricing and burst options to be proposed by Maya; 4) 1-hour head-to-head planned for Tue 07/20 pending Rajiv approval; 5) Eloise to share security pack; 6) Devon to share cost spreadsheet and annotated traces.
[10:22] Rajiv Kapoor: yep that covers it.
[10:25] Hannah Lee: one operational — can you also provide runbook for rollback? we want clear steps.
[10:28] Devon Patel: yes we'll draft a rollback runbook and include it in the playbook doc.
[10:33] Eloise Park: action owners and due dates will be in follow-up email.
[10:37] Tom Alvarez: ok thanks everyone.
[10:40] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and schedule.
[10:44] Rajiv Kapoor: thanks. bye.

Notes: some transcription artifacts present (speaker overlap around 00:28, minor mis-typed acronyms like kv-cash).
